1593

Rome · Legate Filippo Sega

Rome’s instruction to the legate, 14 May 1593

Twelve pages of continuous figures: excommunication, a third party, the Infanta’s claim against the Salic law, fear of Navarre’s “feigned conversion”. A probable and partial decipherment; earlier preliminary reading by Satoshi Tomokiyo (2019).

1532

Ferducci · Fiume

1532 · Ferducci, Fiume — “we shall pretend to go fishing”

Eight enciphered words in a letter otherwise in clear. On 19 July 1532, as Süleyman marched on Vienna, Ferdinand I's agent at Fiume offered to seize the French ambassador at sea on his way back from the sultan — most probably Antonio Rincon. A new reading of an unglossed letter, with a key drawn from contemporary decipherments and confirmed by an independent table of 1542.

Our method →

01 · The document

Start from the signs

Facsimiles and archive references accompany the transcriptions. A graphical resemblance remains a decision to explain.

02 · The reading

Keep the layers distinct

The image, transcribed sign, proposed value and modernised text are separate. Contextual restorations remain visible.

03 · The evidence

Retain the reservations

A coherent sentence does not prove a key. Unresolved points, corrections and earlier work belong in the dossier.
